newsitem.title: FRANCE: Polish PM seeks support from France on NATO, EU.
newsitem.headline: Polish PM seeks support from France on NATO, EU.

text.p: Polish Prime Minister Wladimir Cimoszewicz began a three-day visit to France on Wednesday seeking support for Warsaw's hopes of joining NATO and the European Union.

Cimoszewicz told the French daily Le Monde in an interview this week that he would like to end his visit to Paris "even more convinced that the NATO summit, in July in Madrid, will make concrete decisions on the start of negotiations with Poland...and that in 1998 talks will start on the enlargement of the European Union".
Responding to Cimoszewicz's concern, French Foreign Ministry sources said his discussions in Paris would focus on European security and bilateral issues.

Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said France would reaffirm support for Poland's membership of the EU as early as the year 2000, and he recalled that French President Jacques Chirac had expressed strong support for its admission to NATO during his visit to Warsaw last September.
He said Franco-Polish trade exchanges were booming, with a 47 percent increase last year, making France the third largest investor in Poland and its fourth largest trading partner.

Cimoszewicz said he wanted French business to be even more active in Poland. He also hoped France would help expand the teaching of the French language to compete with successful British and U.S. campaigns to push the English language.
Cimoszewicz was due to meet Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe later in the day, and French businessmen on Thursday.
France has launched an all-out drive to court Eastern Europe. Chirac, who visited Hungary recently, is due to meet Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Sunday and visit Romania next month.
The presidents of Ukraine, Romania, Georgia and Estonia are all due to visit Paris in the next few days.
